messages.subject: Assign value to intervening dates
parts:
I have daily pasture growth rate data calculated at particular dates
over a long time period. This data has been calculated by harvesting
pasture on a particular date, and dividing the growth rate by the
number of days since the last harvest, to estimate the daily growth
rate over that period. I would like to create a table that assigns
this growth rate to each day in the intervening period.

growthrates <- data.frame(dates = as.Date(c(0,35,96,120),origin =
"2000-01-01"), rate = c(NA,30,35,12))

Note the first value is NA, we cannot know the growth rate for the
first harvest, only the second and subsequent.

I would like to end up with
dates rate
2000-01-02 30
2000-01-03 30
2000-01-04 30
....
2000-02-05 30
2000-02-06 35
2000-02-07 35
.... etc.

I have been trying to figure out any way of doing this with loops or
plyr and am rather lost. Does anyone have any suggestions? Thankyou.

messages.author: 0c39e60ddb38622b
messages.subject: Re: Assign value to intervening dates
parts:
Hi Sam:

There are likely more elegant solutions than this one, but I opted for Q & D:

# Generate a sequence of dates
date <- with(growthrates, seq(dates[1] + 1, dates[nrow(growthrates)]),
by = 'days')
# Generate a corresponding vector of rates
rate <- with(growthrates, rep(rate[-1], diff(dates))
# Put 'em together
df <- data.frame(date, rate)

HTH,
Dennis

PS: Congratulations on the recent birth of your daughter! Hope she's
happy and heathy.
